name: Cables that close a loop
brief:
A data centre has `n` racks, numbered 0 to `n - 1`. Engineers lay network cables in the order of `cables`, a list of pairs `[a, b]` of different racks. A cable is spare when its two racks are already joined, directly or through other racks, by the cables laid before it. Return the positions in `cables` of the spare cables, in order, counting from 0.

Write `loop_cables(n, cables)`.

Example. For `n = 5` and `cables = [[0, 1], [1, 2], [3, 4], [2, 0], [4, 3], [1, 3], [0, 4]]`, the cable `[2, 0]` closes the loop 0, 1, 2 and `[4, 3]` repeats a link. `[1, 3]` joins two groups, after which `[0, 4]` is spare. The answer is `[3, 4, 6]`.
constraints: $1 \le n \le 200{,}000$ racks and at most $250{,}000$ cables. A pair may repeat, either way round.
Near $O(m)$ time is the target for $m$ cables. A search of the racks for every cable is too slow, and so is a chain of parent links followed without shortening.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Keep a parent for each rack, so each group has one root. A cable is spare when both racks have the same root; otherwise hang one root under the other. Point racks at their root as you climb, so later climbs are short.

examples.note: Cable 3 closes the loop 0, 1, 2 and cable 4 repeats `[3, 4]`. Cable 5 joins the two groups, so cable 6 is spare.
Each cable reaches a rack not yet joined, so none is spare.

tests.call: (lambda r: (len(r), sum(r)))(loop_cables(200000, [[i + 1, i] for i in range(199999)] + [[i, 199999 - i] for i in range(50000)]))

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. Unlike the usual task of finding one redundant link, every spare cable is listed in order, so the search must carry on past the first.
notes: Union-find keeps one root per group, and a cable is spare exactly when its racks share a root.
The join must hang one root under the other; pointing the rack itself at the other group loses its old links.
Pointing each rack on a climb at the root keeps climbs short, so the work is close to $O(m)$.

planted.slip: Pointing rack `a` itself at the other group, not its root, cuts `a` off from the racks it was joined to.
Counting only repeated pairs misses a cable that closes a loop through other racks.
A recursive find is right, but a long chain of racks runs it out of call depth.
